Rust is compiled and tested only in CI, as the repository requires.\n\n### Template comparison\n\nNone of the eight `link-foundation/*-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` repositories uses floating `*-latest` runners. The Rust template audits only its root `Cargo.lock` while it also commits `examples/javascript-first/Cargo.lock`. That gap is latent today and is reported as link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#250.\n\n### Reported upstream\n\n- link-assistant/web-capture#191: 2.x engines exclude Node 24 runtimes.\n- link-assistant/hive-mind#4065: the red-draft reason is taken from the newest `*.log`.\n- #1574: the HumanEval regression found while reading the runs (a solver-quality issue, not CI).\n\n### Not changed, by decision\n\nPull requests do not compile Rust, so Rust regressions such as the E0308 that failed the 2026-11-15 dependency run show up first on `main`. Adding the Rust stage to every pull request costs CPU minutes on each one, so the case study records this for the maintainers rather than changing the profile.\n\n### Issue Reference\nFixes [2026-11-16T05:57:33.835Z] [INFO]         "content": "# Instructions for AI agents working on formal-ai\n\nThis file is for any automated contributor, such as Claude Code, Codex, the\nhive-mind `solve` command or Formal AI itself. `CLAUDE.md` points here.\n[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) still applies in full. This file restates\nonly the rules an agent breaks most often, because each one has cost real CI\ntime ([issue #1191](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1191)).\n\n## The single push gate\n\nA push starts several workflows at once. Each push that only fixes part of the\nprevious run's failures pays for the whole matrix again. Pull request #1188\nneeded 100 commits and 11 `CI/CD Pipeline` runs, and none of them was green.\nThe rules below make every push count:\n\n1. **Drafting sub-agents never push.** A sub-agent that drafts code, tests or\n   documentation commits locally (or hands its diff back) and stops there.\n   Only the coordinating agent touches the remote.\n2. **One CI/CD agent pushes, once per round.** Exactly one agent owns pushes to\n   the branch. It pushes only after it has collected every actionable failure\n   of the latest run on the current head, and fixed all of them in the same\n   batch.\n3. **Never push while a run is in progress on the branch.** Check first:\n\n   ```bash\n   gh run list --branch \"$(git branch --show-current)\" --status in_progress --json databaseId,workflowName\n   gh run list --branch \"$(git branch --show-current)\" --status queued --json databaseId,workflowName\n   ```\n\n   Both lists must be empty, or must hold only runs for an older head that you\n   are deliberately superseding. Otherwise, keep drafting while the run\n   finishes, then collect its failures (rule 2).\n4. **Run the JavaScript checks locally before the push.** Two kinds of check\n   apply:\n   - the test files next to the change, run one at a time:\n     `timeout 600 node --test --test-concurrency=1 <file>`;\n   - the gates the change touches. These run in JavaScript and never compile\n     Rust: `node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/local-gates.mjs --only <gate>`.\n\n   `--list` shows every gate. Run the whole set\n   (`node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/local-gates.mjs`) before a push that\n   touches shared data such as `data/meta`. The fast pull-request lane runs the\n   same twins, so a failure here would have failed there too.\n5. **No full local Rust build unless the change is Rust-only.** CI compiles\n   Rust: the focused `native-type-check` job on pull requests, and the full\n   matrix on main. Locally, run `rustfmt --check <file>` on the files you\n   changed. That command needs no build.\n6. **If a change is Rust-only and you must build locally, keep the build\n   bounded.** Use one shared target directory for every worktree and agent,\n   with no incremental cache, few jobs, and a prune afterwards:\n\n   ```bash\n   export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=\"$HOME/.cache/formal-ai-target\"  # one directory, shared by all worktrees\n   export CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0                               # no incremental cache to grow without bound\n   export CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2                                # a limited -j for plain cargo commands\n   CARGO_TEST_JOBS=2 scripts/cargo-test.sh --test unit <filter>  # one module, -j 2, then prunes\n   scripts/prune-build-cache.sh                             # prunes old artifacts after any other cargo command\n   ```\n\n   `scripts/prune-build-cache.sh` follows `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. [2026-11-16T05:57:33.835Z] [INFO]     "stdout": "# Instructions for AI agents working on formal-ai\n\nThis file is for any automated contributor, such as Claude Code, Codex, the\nhive-mind `solve` command or Formal AI itself. `CLAUDE.md` points here.\n[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) still applies in full. This file restates\nonly the rules an agent breaks most often, because each one has cost real CI\ntime ([issue #1191](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1191)).\n\n## The single push gate\n\nA push starts several workflows at once. Each push that only fixes part of the\nprevious run's failures pays for the whole matrix again. Pull request #1188\nneeded 100 commits and 11 `CI/CD Pipeline` runs, and none of them was green.\nThe rules below make every push count:\n\n1. **Drafting sub-agents never push.** A sub-agent that drafts code, tests or\n   documentation commits locally (or hands its diff back) and stops there.\n   Only the coordinating agent touches the remote.\n2. **One CI/CD agent pushes, once per round.** Exactly one agent owns pushes to\n   the branch. It pushes only after it has collected every actionable failure\n   of the latest run on the current head, and fixed all of them in the same\n   batch.\n3. **Never push while a run is in progress on the branch.** Check first:\n\n   ```bash\n   gh run list --branch \"$(git branch --show-current)\" --status in_progress --json databaseId,workflowName\n   gh run list --branch \"$(git branch --show-current)\" --status queued --json databaseId,workflowName\n   ```\n\n   Both lists must be empty, or must hold only runs for an older head that you\n   are deliberately superseding. Otherwise, keep drafting while the run\n   finishes, then collect its failures (rule 2).\n4. **Run the JavaScript checks locally before the push.** Two kinds of check\n   apply:\n   - the test files next to the change, run one at a time:\n     `timeout 600 node --test --test-concurrency=1 <file>`;\n   - the gates the change touches. These run in JavaScript and never compile\n     Rust: `node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/local-gates.mjs --only <gate>`.\n\n   `--list` shows every gate. Run the whole set\n   (`node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/local-gates.mjs`) before a push that\n   touches shared data such as `data/meta`. The fast pull-request lane runs the\n   same twins, so a failure here would have failed there too.\n5. **No full local Rust build unless the change is Rust-only.** CI compiles\n   Rust: the focused `native-type-check` job on pull requests, and the full\n   matrix on main. Locally, run `rustfmt --check <file>` on the files you\n   changed. That command needs no build.\n6. **If a change is Rust-only and you must build locally, keep the build\n   bounded.** Use one shared target directory for every worktree and agent,\n   with no incremental cache, few jobs, and a prune afterwards:\n\n   ```bash\n   export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=\"$HOME/.cache/formal-ai-target\"  # one directory, shared by all worktrees\n   export CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0                               # no incremental cache to grow without bound\n   export CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2                                # a limited -j for plain cargo commands\n   CARGO_TEST_JOBS=2 scripts/cargo-test.sh --test unit <filter>  # one module, -j 2, then prunes\n   scripts/prune-build-cache.sh                             # prunes old artifacts after any other cargo command\n   ```\n\n   `scripts/prune-build-cache.sh` follows `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. They pass in CI on this branch.\n\n### 4.2 Rust tests that disagreed with JS (`67558abc1`)\n\n- **A5:** the Rust `gh` work-item read used `normalized_payload`. That function drops a body quoting `exit 5` or `HTTP 403` (issue 1488) as if the command had failed. JS (`js/agentic/progress.mjs`) uses `observed_payload`, and Rust now does too.\n- **A6:** since #1560, a fetched issue body no longer refuses reads, so the issue 698 driver plans `read_file`. The Rust assertion still expected the old plan. The JS planner plans the same three steps (`experiments/issue-1571/a6-driver.mjs`), so the assertion was stale.\n\n### 4.3 Layered CI js-tier group overrun (`f83f2eee1`)\n\nRun 43730269695 recorded durations for only 305 of the 853 suite files. The planner gave unrecorded files 0.1 s, so several 70–150 s files landed in group 7, which then hit its 360 s budget.\n\nThere were two causes:\n\n1. `data/meta/javascript-test-durations.lino` was never refreshed from CI.\n2. Newer `gh` refuses ANSI-coloured job logs unless `--allow-escape-sequences` is passed. Without it, `ci-durations.mjs --tests` and `--playwright-files` measured nothing and said nothing (a false negative of the measuring tool).\n\n**Fix:** `ci-durations.mjs --javascript-ci-logs` folds the `[test-file] duration_ms` lines of a run into the table. Every log read now passes `--allow-escape-sequences`, and skipped jobs are reported.\n\n### 4.4 Hive Mind draft explains a red run with the wrong log (`1711797eb`)\n\nThe shared runner explains a failed draft with the newest `*.log` in the session directory. `capture-draft-command.mjs` rewrote `attempt.log` and `attempt.{stdout,stderr}.log` on every chunk, so the capture itself was always the newest file. Run 43730396084 reported \"docker run exited 5 without a session log error\" instead of \"Finished without changes\".\n\n**Fix:** the capture is now named `attempt.capture.jsonl` plus `attempt.{stdout,stderr}.txt`. A regression test replays the runner's newest-`*.log` selection. The runner-side contract is reported as hive-mind#4065 (§8).\n\n### 4.5 Learning cycle exits 101 with no message (`a1309e282`)\n\nThe workflow wrote stderr to `run.log`, and the `cat` that would print it never ran under `set -e`. `Swatinem/rust-cache` looked for a root `Cargo.toml`, `cargo metadata` failed, and a cache of about 0 MB was saved.\n\n**Fix:** set `workspaces: rust`, and print stderr in a trap that runs on every exit.\n\n### 4.6 Build metadata written into `Cargo.toml` (`bcf1792c5`)\n\ncrates.io reports `toml_edit` as `0.25.19+spec-1.1.0`, and `--apply` wrote that string verbatim. As a result, every cargo invocation of the daily run warned that the metadata \"will be ignored\" (SemVer 2.0.0 §10).\n\n**Fix:** strip `+…` before writing a Cargo or npm requirement, with a parser test.\n\n### 4.7 Issue 1028 ladder budget (`0e5a9f5cd`)\n\nThe weekly step-budget audit failed. A two-leaf ladder leg used 1196 s of its 1200 s budget because the first leaf compiled the crate cold while sccache rejected 706 of 877 writes (run 42472083551).\n\n**Fix:** run one leg per depth-5 leaf (32 legs). Each leg keeps the 1200 s budget, which is 67% of the 30-minute job cap.\n\n### 4.8 Floating runner labels (`4e0805a73`)\n\nEvery job on `main` at `7837d50` carried the notice that `ubuntu-latest` moves to Ubuntu 26 from 2026-10-19 (actions/runner-images#14748), 95 in all. A floating label lets the image change without a commit, so a toolchain difference shows up as an unexplained red run.\n\n**Fix:** pin `ubuntu-24.04` and `windows-2025`. The release matrix keeps `os: ubuntu-latest` only as the leg's *name*, because job names, duration data and the `unit-tests-<os>` checks depend on it, and maps it to the pinned image in `runs-on`.\n\nThree things followed from the pin:\n\n- The canonical release original `original-release-workflow.yml` was exactly at its 1500-line cap. A three-line comment pushed it to 1503 lines, and the fast lint on `ec8562ef5` failed (run 43741781733). The comment is now a trailing comment on the `runs-on` line. The sha in `stage-source-coverage.json` is refreshed, and the projections are regenerated with `generate-staged-release.mjs --write --deployed`. `--check-deployed` passes.\n- Three tests pin reviewed digests or structures of jobs whose only change is the runner: `ci-fast-critical-profile`, `verify-public-release-downloads` and `browser-engine-release-integration`. They keep their reviewed baselines. Each now asserts that the job runs on `ubuntu-24.04`, then checks the baseline with only that field restored. Restoring it reproduces each baseline hash exactly, so the pin is the only difference.\n- The pull-request CI did not run these JavaScript tests (§5.1). They were run locally, one file at a time.\n\n### 4.9 `@link-assistant/web-capture` 2.x on Node 24 runtimes (`ec8562ef5`)\n\nThe daily dependency run moved web-capture to 2.x in the desktop and VS Code manifests. web-capture 2.0.0–2.0.2 declares `engines.node >=26.10.0`, set in its commit `b055a3058` \"refresh locked tooling\". The runtimes that load it are older:\n\n- Electron 44 embeds Node 24: 44.0.0 has 24.18.1, the locked 44.9.3 has 24.22.0, and the newest 44.11.3 has 24.22.2 (releases.electronjs.org);\n- VS Code runs extensions on Node 24;\n- the desktop build uses Node 22.\n\nnpm printed `EBADENGINE` twice. That is only a warning, so the run would have shipped an incompatible pin (a false positive).\n\n**Fix:**\n\n- Both manifests carry the repository's blocked-pin convention (`\"@link-assistant/web-capture//\": \"blocked: …/web-capture/issues/191 (…)\"`), which `scripts/check-dependencies-latest-parsers.rs` already honours.\n- `rust/tests/web/issue-1571-workflow-diagnostics.test.mjs` parses every runtime entry of both lockfiles and fails when an `engines.node` floor is above Node 24.21.0, which is what Electron 44.7.0 embeds (the `^44.7.0` floor in `desktop/package.json`).\n- I verified that the test fails when the lock's web-capture engine is set to `>=26.10.0`.\n\nThe governed specification witness (`experiments/…/unicode-identifier-identity/governed-baseline.v8`) embeds the exact bytes and sha256 of both manifests. Layered CI for `ec8562ef5` was superseded before its JavaScript shards finished, so the stale witness first failed on `dec1acfdb` (run 43743807130: `rust-specification-fixture-integrity` and `rust-specification-unicode-identifiers`).\n\nBefore refreshing it, `experiments/issue-1571/governed-witness-delta.mjs` listed every field that differs between the committed witness and a regenerated one. The 16 differences are the `desktop/package.json` and `vscode/package.json` hashes, plus the eight cases that embed those files' text. The committed text matched `main`'s manifests byte for byte. The witness was then rewritten with the test's own `--refresh-reviewed-baseline` mode, and the delta is now 0.\n\n### 4.10 Cargo audit read one lock of two (`be46692e3`)\n\n`scripts/check-rust-dependencies.sh` audited only `rust/Cargo.lock`. The committed issue #1017 reproducer `experiments/issue-1017-meta-language-quadratic/Cargo.lock` had:\n\n- rustls 0.23.43 (Dependabot alerts 289–292);\n- the yanked chacha20 0.10.1;\n- advisories in quinn-proto, quinn-udp, rustix and webpki-root-certs.\n\nThe Security workflow stayed green (a false negative), and its sparse checkout (`/Cargo.lock`) did not even fetch the file.\n\n**Fix:**\n\n- The script discovers locks with `git ls-files -- 'Cargo.lock' '*/Cargo.lock'`.\n- It fails when a committed lock was not checked out.\n- The shipped lock keeps `--deny warnings`. Unshipped locks fail on `vulnerabilities`, `unsound` and `yanked`.\n- An `unmaintained` notice with no fixed release (`unsafe-libyaml`, pulled in by the pinned meta-language 0.58.1) is printed but does not fail. Ignoring it would need a blocked-upstream proof, and a reproducer pinned to a historical version is not shipped.\n- The reproducer's crates are updated (`cargo update -p`).\n- The sparse-checkout pattern is now `Cargo.lock`, which matches at any depth. `fast-pull-request-production-profile.test.mjs` asserts with real `git sparse-checkout check-rules` that every committed `Cargo.lock` is selected.\n\n## 5. Run 40307862657 (10-26, sha c4137c0e7, job 121521364735): FP with an FN-risk, NOT FIXED\n\n```\n562: Sampling up to 400 runs of link-assistant/formal-ai on main.\n...\n569:   ... 175 runs\n586: ##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.\n595: ## Step budget headroom\n604: | 1.7% (loose) | 600 | 10 | 16 | Publish source networks | packets | ... |\n607: Nothing ran these, so nothing knows whether their budgets are the right size.\n609–637: (every other budget, 29 of them, listed as \"no observation in this window\")\n```\n\nStep conclusions from the API: \"Collect measured job durations\" failure; \"Check every\ndeclared cap\" **skipped**; \"Check every declared budget\" **success**.\n\n- **Root cause**: `scripts/collect-job-durations.sh:91-102` runs\n  `gh api --paginate .../runs/<id>/jobs ... 2>/dev/null | while read ...` under\n  `set -euo pipefail`. Somewhere between run 175 and run 200, one `gh api` call\n  failed, most likely a transient 5xx or secondary rate limit. `pipefail` plus\n  `set -e` then ended the script with exit 1, and `2>/dev/null` had already thrown\n  away the only message. The comment above it assumes that runs past retention\n  \"return an empty list rather than an error\", but it does not cover transport\n  errors.\n- **FN-risk**: the step-budget audit has `if: always()`. It ran on an almost empty\n  TSV (1 observed budget out of 30) and reported **success**. The cap audit, which\n  lacks `if: always()`, was skipped. If the collector had exited 0 with a partial\n  sample, both audits would have been green with almost nothing measured.\n- **Fixed?** No. The collector is unchanged since 707de6bc4 (09-07).\n- **Proposed minimal fix** (`scripts/collect-job-durations.sh`):\n  - Retry each per-run `gh api` call 3 times with backoff.\n  - On final failure, print `::warning::could not read jobs of run <id>: <gh stderr>`\n    and count it, instead of `2>/dev/null` plus abort.\n  - Exit 1 only if more than 5% of sampled runs failed.\n  - End stdout with a trailer row such as `#complete\\t<count>\\t<failed>`.\n  - In `check-step-budget-headroom.rs` and `check-job-headroom.rs`, refuse a verdict\n    (exit 1 with a named error) when the trailer is missing or the observed fraction\n    is below a floor.\n- **Regression test**: a test (e.g. in `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/job_budget_fit.rs`, which\n  already covers this collector) that puts a fake `gh` on `PATH` that fails once for\n  one run id. Assert that the collector exits 0, prints the warning naming the run and\n  the gh error, and still emits the other runs' rows. A second case feeds a TSV with\n  no trailer to `check-step-budget-headroom.rs` and asserts non-zero.\n\n### 5c. It does not check it against the time the run has left. So under a hard deadline, `solve` spends minutes sleeping, and it can start a sleep that cannot finish before the deadline.\n\n## Evidence\n\nRun: link-assistant/formal-ai Hive Mind draft run [43738765561](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/43738765561). The process is killed during the second wait, without a third attempt.\n\n## Workaround\n\nNone from the calling workflow: `formal-ai-draft.mjs` forwards only `GH_TOKEN` and `FORMAL_AI_INSTALL_GRANT`, and the run-context variables, into the container. So `HIVE_MIND_MIN_TRANSIENT_ERROR_DELAY_MS` cannot be lowered for a draft.\n\n## Suggested fix\n\n1. Let `solve` take a wall-clock deadline: a `--deadline-at` flag, or an environment variable that `formal-ai-draft.mjs` sets from its own budget.\n2. In `createTransientRetryBudget().evaluate`, refuse a delay that would end past that deadline, using a new reason `deadline`, so the run fails fast with a clear message.\n3. Alternatively, cap `minDelayMs` at a fraction of the remaining time when `HIVE_MIND_EPHEMERAL_CONTAINER=1`.\n4.
